Who it's for — and who it's not for

For you if: you're starting a pressure washing or exterior cleaning business — or you started one and you're running it on memory, texts, and a notebook. Solo operators and small crews. If your paperwork is currently "I'll figure it out when it comes up," this is the shortcut.

Not for you if: you're buying into a franchise (they hand you their systems), you need jurisdiction-specific legal documents drafted for your state (that's an attorney, and worth it), or you want a marketing course. This is paperwork and pricing infrastructure — it won't get you clients, it makes you ready for the ones you get.

FAQ

Can I edit the templates? Yes — every file is fully editable. Replace the placeholders with your business name, adjust the terms and the rates, and use them as your own. That's the whole point.

Are these legal documents? No. They're business templates written from operating experience, and they're a far better starting point than a blank page. Contract law varies by state, so have a local attorney review anything you'll rely on — particularly the waiver.

Will the pricing calculator work in my market? The defaults are sane 2026 US suburban starting points, and every rate is a yellow cell you can change: target hourly rate, production rates by service type, condition factors, and your minimum job floor. Time yourself on your first ten jobs and put your real numbers in — that's what makes it yours.

Do I need special software? No. Word and Excel work, and so do the free Google and Apple equivalents.

Is this the same as the cleaning kit? No. Same operating philosophy, entirely different trade. The pricing model is built on surface area and production rates, the checklists are soft-wash and flatwork procedures, and the waiver addresses the damage claims specific to putting water on somebody's building.

Templates are starting points, not legal advice. Have a local attorney review contracts before use.
